topics.label: Sick-day care

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

topics.scope: Prepare for ordinary sick days at home: food, everyday comforts, contact, appointment logistics and pet care. No treatment, symptom assessment or urgent response.

concerns.label: Someone to check in on me
Daily tasks when I need to rest

guidance: Prepare useful options in advance. Do not assess symptoms or suggest medication, remedies or delaying care.
Prepare before a future sick day. Start with existing supplies; service research is allowed without booking or payment. Respect explicit budget and support limits.
A directory result is only a research lead. Check eligibility, costs and availability directly; do not promise help.
Care-contact and travel tasks are administrative preparation for nonurgent appointments, not decisions about when or where to seek urgent care.
Only suggest pet tasks when the person selects the pet concern. Never assume a pet from living alone.
Keep chosen concerns in charge. Return fewer useful actions when the library cannot support three distinct fits.

resources.name: 211 — local community resources

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

resources.purpose: Find your local US 211 to research practical community support, including food and transportation assistance.
resources.limits: 211 provides information and referrals, not a booked service. Eligibility, prices and availability of referred programs vary. No check-in or emergency response is promised.

resources.name: Rover — pet sitter research

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

resources.purpose: Compare potential paid drop-in sitters for cats or dogs in your area before you need one.
resources.limits: Research is free; bookings cost money. Coverage, prices, pet types, experience and dates vary. A listing is not a confirmed booking or guarantee of suitability.

resources.name: Taskrabbit — shopping and errands
resources.purpose: Research paid practical help such as collecting dry cleaning or getting everyday supplies in supported locations.
resources.limits: Check coverage, included work, total charges and booking notice. No availability or suitability guarantee. Research does not book a service.

resources.name: Pet Sitters International — sitter finder
resources.purpose: Find member pet-care businesses to contact about future drop-in care, experience with the pet, notice and an introductory meeting.
resources.limits: PSI does not inspect or endorse listed businesses. Ask the provider about fees, visit notice, meeting first, and what happens if they cannot attend. A lead or inquiry is not agreed care.

resources.name: HHS — finding telehealth
resources.purpose: Find routes to virtual care through an insurer or a health center without assuming an existing doctor.
resources.limits: Information guide, not a care provider. Confirm eligible services, first-patient access, regional availability and personal cost with the plan or provider. Insurance coverage does not mean a visit is free.

resources.name: Teladoc — benefits and access FAQ
resources.purpose: Understand how an employer or health plan may provide virtual care and how to check eligibility.
resources.limits: Teladoc is an example, not known to be in this user's plan. Use the service actually named by her benefits. Service eligibility and fees vary. Do not promise free care or copy a headline price.

resources.name: HRSA — Find a Health Center
resources.purpose: Find community health centers serving people with or without health insurance or ability to pay.
resources.limits: Directory, not a confirmed appointment or free-care guarantee. Ask the center about new patients, current fees or reduced-fee eligibility, and whether a first visit can be virtual.

resources.name: One Medical — On-Demand Care
resources.purpose: Research a self-pay one-time virtual-care option when there is no applicable insurance benefit.
resources.limits: On-Demand Care does not accept insurance; scheduled visits have different billing. Confirm current price, state eligibility, scope and any additional charges directly. Do not promise a prescription, suitability, a lowest price or that a membership covers all care.

actions.outcome: Two easy food options are noted, including what you have and anything missing.

task.title: Give tomorrow-you two easy food options
task.summary: Pick familiar food you’d actually want, so a low-energy day involves one less decision.
steps: Look over food you already have or usually keep at home.
Choose two familiar options that take little preparation; note any ingredient missing from what you have.
Save their names and locations in your usual note, with missing ingredients on your next shopping list.
task.done_when: Two easy food options are noted, including what you have and anything missing.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: Your everyday comforts are together, with missing items noted.

task.title: Give your resting spot a little setup
task.summary: Keep everyday comforts close, using a shelf or basket and things you already own.
steps: Choose a reachable shelf or basket near where you like to rest.
Gather tissues, a charging cable and another everyday comfort you already use; keep the cable out of walking paths.
Put them together and note any missing item for your next usual shopping trip.
task.done_when: Your everyday comforts are together, with missing items noted.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: A relevant service contact, or your local 211 contact, is saved with a specific question.

task.title: Find one local place to ask for help
task.summary: You don’t need a nearby friend to start looking for support. Find a real contact and learn what they can offer.
steps: Use the linked 211 finder to open your local directory or find its contact details.
Look for your chosen need: food, a check-in, or practical help. Check eligibility, coverage, costs and how to request it.
Save one relevant contact and your next question. If none fits, save the local 211 contact to ask about alternatives.
task.done_when: A relevant service contact, or your local 211 contact, is saved with a specific question.

resources.why: Find your local directory or referral team; ask what practical help matches your need and eligibility.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: Your request is sent and clearly marked as agreed or awaiting a reply.
prerequisites: A person the user already knows and feels comfortable contacting; no nearby helper is required.

task.title: Make a check-in feel easy to ask for
task.summary: If there’s someone you’d like to hear from, a simple agreement can make staying in touch easier—even from far away.
steps: Choose someone you already know and feel comfortable asking; they don’t need to live nearby.
Ask whether a short text or call at a time you choose would work on a future sick day.
Save their reply and the agreed time, or mark the plan as waiting for a reply. No automatic monitoring is involved.
task.done_when: Your request is sent and clearly marked as agreed or awaiting a reply.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: One clinic’s appointment contact and any unanswered practical questions are saved.

task.title: Put appointment details where you’ll find them
task.summary: A little admin now can spare you a search later. Keep a nonurgent appointment contact easy to reach.
steps: Open the official website of a clinic you use or would consider for a future nonurgent appointment.
Find its appointment phone number or booking page, opening hours, and any new-patient or payment information you need.
Save those details in your usual contacts or note; mark anything you still need to confirm with the clinic.
task.done_when: One clinic’s appointment contact and any unanswered practical questions are saved.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: A possible round trip is saved, or a specific transport question is ready for the clinic.

task.title: Work out a future appointment trip
task.summary: Map one realistic way to get to a nonurgent appointment, without assuming a car or someone available to drive.
steps: Choose a clinic you use or would consider, and look up one travel option you could realistically use.
Check the provider’s own information for cost, booking notice, accessibility and how you would get home.
Save the route or booking contact and any unanswered question. If nothing fits, note the gap to ask the clinic about.
task.done_when: A possible round trip is saved, or a specific transport question is ready for the clinic.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: A private everyday-care note is ready to share with a helper you choose.

task.title: Leave your pet’s routine ready to share
task.summary: Make it easier for a future helper to follow the ordinary routine your pet already knows.
steps: Write your pet’s usual food, feeding times, water routine and everyday needs without changing their existing care.
Note where the everyday supplies are and add your usual vet’s contact details.
Save the note privately where you can share it with an agreed helper; leave keys, codes and home-entry details out.
task.done_when: A private everyday-care note is ready to share with a helper you choose.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: One potential sitter and a question are saved, or the care gap is clearly noted.
prerequisites: Research applies to cats or dogs; another pet type needs a suitable specialist.

task.title: Find a pet sitter worth contacting
task.summary: For a cat or dog, compare one possible paid helper now. You’re researching a future option, not booking care today.
steps: Open the linked sitter search and look for drop-in visits in your area for your cat or dog.
Compare relevant pet experience, recent reviews, total fees and cancellation terms; treat calendar availability as something to confirm.
Save one profile and a question to ask before a meet-and-greet. If none fits, note that care is still unarranged.
task.done_when: One potential sitter and a question are saved, or the care gap is clearly noted.

resources.why: Research paid drop-in sitters, compare fit and fees, then confirm availability directly before arranging care.

purchase_checks: Confirm experience with your pet and its routine.
Check total fees, cancellation terms and confirmed dates.
task.no_purchase_option: You can prepare the pet-care note without booking or paying anyone.

review.author: assistant
review.scope: Preventive everyday preparation; no clinical or emergency guidance.

actions.outcome: One nonessential chore is rescheduled or removed from your usual reminder.

task.title: Give one nonessential chore a day off
task.summary: Make a little room for rest. Choose one ordinary job that can wait without creating another problem.
steps: Choose one nonessential chore, such as folding clean laundry. Leave care duties and time-sensitive responsibilities out.
Move it to a later day you choose, or remove it if it no longer matters.
Update your usual reminder or note so you don’t need to keep it in mind.
task.done_when: One nonessential chore is rescheduled or removed from your usual reminder.
